name: SigmaCLI
observations: npm package name: sigma-cli
Current version: 0.9.0
Binary: sigma — pattern: sigma {domain} {action} [options]
TypeScript source compiled to dist/; entry point: bin/sigma.js
Node.js requirement: >=18.0.0
Install globally: npm install -g sigma-cli (or npm link from local source if not published)
Version is defined in src/config.ts SIGMA_VERSION and package.json version — both must stay in sync
Source repo: sigma-ecosystem (TypeScript/Node.js npm package implementing the Sigma governance protocol)
Source: package.json, src/config.ts, SIGMA_PROTOCOL.md Section 22

name: SigmaSkillFiles
observations: 32 skill files total: 4 platforms × 8 skills (arc, fmn, dev, aud, checkpoint, cso, report, sigma-test)
Platform claude_code: ~/.claude/commands/ with .md extension — invoked as /arc /fmn /dev /aud /checkpoint /cso /report /sigma-test
Platform codex: ~/.codex/skills/ with no extension — invoked as #arc #fmn etc.
Platform reasonix: ~/.reasonix/skills/ with .md extension
Platform antigravity: ~/.gemini/agents/ with .md extension
Source files: setup/targets/{platform}/ in sigma-ecosystem repo
ROLE_FILES map in src/commands/setup.ts defines platform→role→filename mapping
/report is universal read-only Director briefing; NOT a governance role; does not switch roles; chat-only output
/report word limits: 300 default, 150 with --brief flag, 500 with --full flag
/sigma-test is universal read-only diagnostic skill; checks CLI, MCP, memory, skill files, global setup, and project structure; outputs PASS/WARN/FAIL table
ARC/FMN/DEV skill files include Cross-Role CSO Check section after Bootstrap Protocol
AUD skill files include External Audit CSO Scope section instead of Cross-Role CSO Check
Governance roles (ARC/FMN/DEV/AUD) have 4-step Bootstrap Protocol (AUD uses 3-step passive bootstrap)
sigma setup install deploys 8 skill files per detected platform interactively; --yes flag is non-interactive
Source: SIGMA_PROTOCOL.md Section 25.4, src/commands/setup.ts ROLE_FILES

name: SigmaSetup
observations: Global dir: ~/.sigma/ — contains templates/, rules/, governance/, bridge/, projects.json, sigma.config.json, memory_sigma.jsonl
sigma setup install: creates ~/.sigma/ structure; copies templates/rules/constitution/protocol; deploys 7 skill files per platform; deploys hook guard (Claude Code only)
sigma setup update: refreshes ~/.sigma/ templates/rules/governance only — does NOT redeploy skill files to AI tool directories
sigma setup memory: creates .mcp.json in project dir; creates ~/.sigma/memory_sigma.jsonl if absent; seeds it from bundle if empty; prints MCP config snippet
sigma setup memory --vscode: also writes .vscode/mcp.json for VS Code extension
sigma setup memory --reseed: overwrites memory_sigma.jsonl with fresh seed from package bundle regardless of existing content
Memory seed bundled at setup/sigma-memory-seed.jsonl inside the npm package
Hook guard: setup/targets/hooks/protect-sigma.js — blocks direct edits to Sigma/progress.json via PreToolUse hook in ~/.claude/settings.json
sigma project start --id ID --name 'Name': creates Sigma/ folder, progress.json, bridge files, AND .mcp.json at project root; seeds memory_sigma.jsonl if absent; registers in ~/.sigma/projects.json
Project ID rules: uppercase letters, digits, hyphens only; max 12 characters
sigma project sync --confirm: updates governance files inside an existing project from current package
Source: SIGMA_PROTOCOL.md Section 25.2, src/commands/setup.ts

name: SigmaLifecycle
observations: Four phases: START → DESIGN → BUILD → CLOSE
DESIGN phase: ARC drafts DIR-INTENT; complete when DIR-INTENT LOCKED
BUILD phase: FMN drafts FMN-PLAN (locked before DEV begins); DEV drafts DEV-EXEC; iterative
CLOSE phase: Director authors DIR-CLOSE with explicit PLAN and EXEC version references
Gate 1: DIR-INTENT LOCKED required before sigma plan new
Gate 2: FMN-PLAN LOCKED required before sigma exec new
Gate 3: full INTENT→PLAN→EXEC LOCKED chain required before sigma close new
Artifact versioning — Tier 1 (DIR-INTENT, DIR-CLOSE, ROADMAP): v1.0/v1.1/v2.0, single-active, auto-supersede
Artifact versioning — Tier 2 (FMN-PLAN, DEV-EXEC): v0.1/v0.2/v0.3, multi-active, manual supersede only
Artifact versioning — Tier L (CSO): timestamp in filename, immutable log entry
STALE_INTENT: FMN-PLAN or DEV-EXEC referencing a superseded DIR-INTENT; sigma close new requires --ack-stale-intent flag
Roles: ARC (DESIGN), FMN (BUILD), DEV (BUILD), AUD (advisory, all phases)
Role immutability: cannot switch between ARC/FMN/DEV/AUD within a session; new session required
Director is sole lock authority — no AI role may lock any artifact without explicit Director authorization
Source: SIGMA_PROTOCOL.md Sections 3, 4, 6, 7, 8, 11

name: SigmaCSO
observations: CSO = Cognitive State Object; optional artifact for preserving session context between agent sessions
Naming: CSO-{ROLE}-{YYYYMMDD}-{HHMM}.md — stored in Sigma/logs/
Creation path 1: /checkpoint skill → Source: CHECKPOINT (quick state preservation, lower priority in cross-role review)
Creation path 2: /cso skill → Source: CSO (formal handoff, higher priority in cross-role review)
sigma cso new (no --from): copies CSO-TEMPLATE.md; sufficient to ensure metadata is present
sigma cso new --from <draft>: bypasses template; skill must verify draft contains CSO Metadata section before using --from
CSO Metadata 6 fields: Source | Created By Role | Purpose | Related Artifact | Related Artifact State | Authority Level
Authority Level: ALWAYS Context Only — never overrides locked artifacts or progress.json
Cross-Role CSO Check — ARC reads: CSO-AUD-, CSO-FMN- prefix files
Cross-Role CSO Check — FMN reads: CSO-ARC-, CSO-AUD-, CSO-FMN- prefix files
Cross-Role CSO Check — DEV reads: CSO-FMN-, CSO-AUD-, CSO-DEV- prefix files
Cross-Role CSO Check logic: Collect by prefix → Prioritize Source:CSO over Source:CHECKPOINT → Filter by Related Artifact vs active version → Cap at 3
AUD does NOT independently scan Sigma/logs/ for CSO files; reads only what Director explicitly provides or authorizes
If CSO conflicts with locked artifacts or progress.json: locked artifacts win; report conflict to Director; never silently resolve
Source: SIGMA_PROTOCOL.md Section 18, Sigma/rules/ARC-RULE.md, FMN-RULE.md, DEV-RULE.md, AUD-RULE.md

name: SigmaMemoryArchitecture
observations: Two-tier memory model: project decision log + global memory
Tier 1 — Sigma/memory/decisions.jsonl: per-project, CLI-written on lock events only, agents read but do not write
Tier 2 — ~/.sigma/memory_sigma.jsonl: global cross-project, written by agents via MCP tools, Director-approved items only
MCP server for global memory: sigma-memory (@modelcontextprotocol/server-memory); memory file: ~/.sigma/memory_sigma.jsonl
MCP server for planning: sequential-thinking (@modelcontextprotocol/server-sequential-thinking)
Both MCP servers configured via .mcp.json in project root (created by sigma setup memory)
Memory promotion boundary: only generalizable/reusable knowledge goes to global memory; project-specific stays in decisions.jsonl or CSO artifacts
No auto-promotion: no CLI command or lock event automatically writes to memory_sigma.jsonl
Mandatory bootstrap for governance roles: search_nodes({ query: 'sigma ecosystem constants' }) + read_graph()
Source: SIGMA_PROTOCOL.md Section 24

name: SigmaCLICommands
observations: Domains: project, session, intent, plan, exec, close, roadmap, git, cso, setup, gitignore
sigma session bootstrap [--role ARC|AUD|FMN|DEV]: outputs lifecycle phase, artifact states, gate status, recent CSOs, next valid ops
sigma intent: new | review | lock | status | list
sigma plan: new | audit | lock | supersede --v <ver> --reason '...' | status | list
sigma exec: new | audit | advance (building|testing|complete) | lock | supersede | status | list
sigma close: new [--ack-stale-intent] | audit | lock | status
sigma roadmap: new | lock | list
sigma git evidence: read-only; outputs branch, latest commit, changed files, diff stat
sigma cso new [--role <role>] [--from <file>]: creates CSO file in Sigma/logs/; registers in progress.json

Command authority classes: Read-only (any role) | Draft/Operational (within role boundary) | Advisory (Director-triggered) | Approval (explicit Director authorization required) | Risk/Supersession (explicit Director authorization required)
Lock commands always require explicit Director authorization: approved / lock it / go ahead / run it / confirmed
Ambiguous signals not sufficient for lock: okay / noted / makes sense / looks good
Source: SIGMA_PROTOCOL.md Section 23, Section 16A

name: SigmaProjectStructure
observations: Sigma/ governance folder at project root — separate from all source code
Sigma/ subfolders: design/ (DIR-INTENT), build/ (FMN-PLAN, DEV-EXEC, ROADMAP), close/ (DIR-CLOSE), rules/ (role rules), logs/ (CSO files), memory/ (decisions.jsonl)
Sigma/progress.json: CLI-managed runtime state — agents MUST NOT edit directly; use sigma commands
Sigma/memory/decisions.jsonl: CLI-managed decision log — agents read but do not write
Sigma/rules/ files: ARC-RULE.md, AUD-RULE.md, FMN-RULE.md, DEV-RULE.md — read-only during execution
Sigma/templates/: artifact templates including CSO-TEMPLATE.md with CSO Metadata section
Bridge files at project root: CLAUDE.md (Tier 1 Full), GEMINI.md (Tier 1 Full), AGENTS.md (Tier 1 Full), DEEPSEEK.md (Tier 2 Lightweight), REASONIX.md (Tier 3 Shell Whitelist)
Source code, tests, scripts, and deliverables live OUTSIDE Sigma/ — Sigma governs, does not own work product
sigma-ecosystem is the project where Sigma governs itself: governance terminology may appear in product code by exception
Source: SIGMA_PROTOCOL.md Section 12
